note: Humboldt County Conservation Board park, about 114 acres along the West Fork of the Des Moines River west of Humboldt on Hwy 3, with a boat ramp and dock, about three miles of multiuse trail, an 18-hole disc golf course and two cabins. Camp hosts on site. --Claude
summary: Count corrected 42 -> 55 (adds the 13-site roadside campground at 2210 Sheldon Ave); confirmed $20/$25, FCFS only, Apr 15-Oct 15, 30/50A, full hookups at 5 sites, showers, dump. 11 seasonal sites. River ~50 m wide; no pad found on open bank, so not waterfront stays. Pin fine.
flags: SITES: the stored 42 counted only the lower (14) and upper (28) campgrounds; the county page also lists 'a roadside park and campground' at 2210 Sheldon Ave with 'nine 50amp spots with water hookups and four 30 amp spots without water hookups', so 55. The county's own humboldtcounty.iowa.gov page is stale ('2014 Rates are $15.00 Electric and $10.00 Non-electric', '43 Full Hook-Up Campsites', '12 Primitive Campsites').

WATERFRONT (not waterfront kept; weak riverview lead): the West Fork of the Des Moines is about 45-55 m wide here (riverfront class). The upper campground's pull-through loop sits in an open field ~150 m south of the river behind woods. The lower area by the boat ramp has a gravel lot and a camper beside the access road, 20-30 m from the water behind a wooded strip; I could not pick out its 14 rock pads on Esri imagery and the page has no site map. No open apron seen, so no on-water lead. If the lower pads face the river through the trees, riverview might be earned; unconfirmed.
LONG-STAY: 11 of 55 sites are seasonal ('10 seasonal campsites ... and 1 seasonal campsite'); the rest are first-come nightly. Not a seasonal park.
WEBSITE: the stored website carries both the county page (stale) and mycountyparks; the mycountyparks page is the current one. apply.py does not write website.
PIN fine: the stored pin is on the park road just north of the upper loop, ~50 m from it.
Note: removed the site counts, hookups, rates, booking, season and facilities the fields now hold.
